Here’s a quick rundown of some popular “tools”—both online platforms and developer‑friendly APIs—that you can use to book flights: | Category | Tool / Service | What it offers | |----------|-----------------|---------------| | **Online Booking Sites** | *Expedia*, *Kayak*, *Orbitz*, *Priceline*, *Hotwire* | Full consumer interfaces where users can browse, compare, and purchase tickets directly. | | **Travel Aggregators & Meta‑Search Engines** | *Google Flights*, *Skyscanner*, *Momondo*, *TripAdvisor Flights* | Search multiple airlines simultaneously, show price trends, filter by duration, layovers, etc. | | **Airline Direct Websites** | Individual airline portals (e.g., Delta, United, Lufthansa). | Often have loyalty program integration, seat selection, baggage options, etc. | | **API Platforms (for developers)** | • **Amadeus Self‑Service APIs** – Flight Offers Search, Availability, Pricing.
• **Sabre APIs** – Global Distribution System (GDS) connectivity, inventory, pricing.
• **Travelport Universal API** – Unified interface to GDSs.
• **SkyScanner Rapid API** – Cheap fares, multi-city searches.
• **Kiwi.com API** – Multi‑carrier itineraries, flexible dates.
• **OpenSky API** – Real‑time flight status (not bookings but useful for context).
• **FlightAware API** – Tracking, delays, cancellations. | These allow you to build custom booking flows, retrieve fare quotes, check availability, reserve seats, and even handle payments via partner processors. | | **Payment Gateways & Ticket Issuance Partners** | *Stripe Connect*, *PayPal Adaptive Payments*, *Adyen*, *Worldpay*. | Handle secure payment processing once your app has selected a ticket. Many travel APIs integrate with them out of the box. | | **CRM & Loyalty Integration** | *Salesforce Marketing Cloud*, *HubSpot CRM*, *Microsoft Dynamics 365*. | Store customer profiles, manage frequent flyer miles, push personalized offers. | | **Mobile SDKs** | *Flutter*, *React Native*, *SwiftUI*, *Jetpack Compose* + integrated APIs above. | Build native mobile apps that embed flight search/bookings seamlessly. | ### How to choose? 1. **Consumer vs B2B** - If you’re building a website/app for end‑users, start with meta‑search engines or direct airline partners plus a payment gateway. - If you’re creating a corporate solution or integrating into existing systems, consider full GDS APIs (Sabre, Amadeus, Travelport). 2. **Pricing Model** - Most aggregators charge per click or per lead. - GDS APIs usually bill per transaction or offer subscription plans. 3. **Geographic Coverage** - Check whether the platform covers all regions you target (some focus more on North America, others on Europe/Africa/etc.). 4. **Feature Set Needed** - Do you need dynamic packaging (flight+hotel+car)? Look at Amadeus or Sabre. - Need real‑time seat maps? Airline APIs often expose those. --- #### Quick Start Example (Python) If you’d like to experiment quickly, here’s how you could call the **Skyscanner Rapid API** to fetch cheap round‑trip prices: ```python import requests api_key = "" headers = {"x-apikey": api_key} params = { "country":"US", "currency":"USD", "locale":"en-US", "originPlace":"SFO-sky", "destinationPlace":"LHR-sky", "outboundDate":"2026-07-01", "inboundDate":"2026-07-10", } response = requests.get("https://partners.api.skypicker.com/flights/search", headers=headers, params=params) print(response.json()) ``` Replace `` with your key from the Skyscanner Partner portal. You’ll receive JSON containing flight segments, carriers, prices, and links back to the booking site.
